engagement_title: Harbor Crest Realty listing kit: build the whole of 14 Marlowe Crescent from a room by room capture set, and turn the printer's open house card into a six agent run the brokerage can repeat every listing
vertical: Real Estate, Construction and Property, residential brokerage, nine agents, suburban Calderon County (Rosewood)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork 'Open House Finance Flyer' package post quoted in the ledger, which asks for an editable print and digital flyer set, sophisticated and approachable rather than luxury, with easily editable property photos, purchase price, payment scenarios and contact information. All identifying detail is laundered to fiction: the lender in the real post becomes a brokerage, the market becomes the invented Calderon County with the invented town of Rosewood, and the listing becomes the fictional 14 Marlowe Crescent. Co-anchor: the Upwork high volume real estate photo editing open call, whose named edit list is window pulls, colour correction, vertical alignment, lawn enhancement and general cleanup, whose deliverable is stated as portal ready images with consistent style across each property, and whose stated volume is twenty to forty photos per listing at a twenty four to forty eight hour turnaround. That post named no client, so the brokerage is laundered to the fictional Harbor Crest Realty. Third anchor: the Freelancer.com 'Vibrant Social and Web Graphics' post asking for matching website graphics, hero images, section headers and call to action spots plus banner ads, everything feeling part of one cohesive family while being perfectly sized for its destination, with a mini style reference for colours and typography so future assets stay consistent. Those three posts are the same commission split across three postings: one listing's photography, one listing's collateral, and the reusable basis. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the fuller version honest, because HTML authoring now produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes and a bare press PDF can be reverse engineered into a live merge template.
client_one_liner: Our shooter sends the rooms back exactly as captured and they never look like one house, our printer's open house card has to be reordered one agent at a time, and 14 Marlowe Crescent lists in three weeks.
client_brief:
Harbor Crest Realty, 14 Marlowe Crescent

We are a nine person brokerage in Rosewood, in Calderon County. We list around forty homes a season and we have never had a kit that looks like one firm. 14 Marlowe Crescent is our next listing and we want the kit built on it, because whatever we land here we will reuse on the next forty.

The photographs. Our shooter went room by room and sent everything back exactly as captured. They are competent frames and they are not a set. Some rooms read yellow, one bedroom reads distinctly cool, and the outside was shot a good while after the inside. Buyers scroll these in a row on a phone, so they have to read as one house photographed once, with the verticals straight and the rooms sitting at a sensible size in the frame. The windows matter to us more than anything else, because the garden and the ravine behind it are the reason this house sells. Right now the windows are just bright.

What we need built. The page that sits behind the listing link, with a hero, a gallery and a table of the facts. An open house flyer at A4 that we print ourselves. And the posts the agents put out the day it goes live: one square, one tall for stories, one four by five. All of it editable by us, because in three weeks it is the next listing and the only things that change are the pictures, the address and the numbers.

Separately, the printer's file for our open house card. Six of our agents work open houses and each needs their own card with their photo, name, licence line and direct number. We have the artwork and a roster, and we have been ordering these one at a time.

The house is six hundred and twenty five thousand. Buyers are thirty to forty five making a first move up. Warm and straightforward, not glossy, not luxury. Please send a note on what you did and what we should watch on the next listing.
price_band_and_audience: A 625,000 dollar suburban family home at a 2.5 percent listing side, buyers 30 to 45 making a first move up, agents 35 to 55. The band is load bearing. At this price the grammar is warm and legible: a readable feature table, honest daylight, real room sizes in frame, type that a phone renders cleanly, and an agent's face on the card because the relationship is the product. Push it toward prestige restraint, near black grounds, sparse type and a rates figure hidden in a discreet line and the same house reads as under sold and the buyer assumes something is wrong with it. Push the other way into starburst callouts, three accent colours and every fact shouted and it reads as a distress sale. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even with every technical gate green. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed, often with a per listing repeat rate attached.

brand_identity.sector: Residential real estate brokerage listing family homes across a suburban county.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2011, in Rosewood, Calderon County. A nine-agent brokerage listing around forty homes a season.
brand_identity.about: Harbor Crest Realty is a nine-person residential brokerage in Rosewood, listing suburban family homes for owners and guiding first move-up buyers through them. The firm runs a steady volume of listings a year and wants one repeatable kit that makes every listing look like it came from the same firm.
brand_identity.audience: Move-up buyers aged 30 to 45 making their first step up from a starter home, scrolling listings on a phone. Also the sellers who list with the firm and the six agents who work open houses.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Homes centre on the mid-market, with 14 Marlowe Crescent at 625,000 dollars and a 2.5 percent listing side. Positioned as sophisticated but approachable, not luxury and not discount: warm, legible, honest, with real facts and real room sizes shown plainly.
brand_identity.typography: One warm, legible system that renders cleanly on a phone and on an office printer: a friendly geometric or humanist sans for headings and figures, paired with a readable text face for the facts table and body. Comfortable sizes, clear hierarchy, nothing prestige-cold or shouty.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, welcoming, benefit-led without hype. Speaks like a neighbour who knows the street. Example line: "Four bedrooms, a garden that backs onto the ravine, and an open house this Sunday."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The firm is not rebranding. A current sign and business card are already in the field and are supplied as the basis, so the new kit must match what is out there rather than replace it. The open house card artwork is held by the printer as a press PDF; there is no central brand file beyond the sign and card reference.
brand_identity.values: Consistency across every listing, honesty in the photography, and collateral the brokerage can rebuild itself for the next home. The agent relationship is the product.

assets_supplied.name: marlowe_captures/ (18 frames, 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Room by room listing capture of the whole house plus front and rear exteriors, one pass, handheld on a tripod at chest height, delivered straight off the card with no processing.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything as captured. Some rooms read yellow, one bedroom is cool, and the outside was shot later than the inside."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: On five interior frames the room was exposed for the room, so every window is clipped flat to paper white with nothing behind it, and a highlight move on those frames returns success while the readout is that nothing at all changes. Separately two frames are the same living room from one tripod position a minute apart, and the study named in the facts sheet has no capture at all, which no filename or count reveals.

assets_supplied.name: harbor_crest_open_house_card.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The brokerage's existing open house card exactly as its printer holds it: a real press PDF, one card per page, agent photograph at the top, then name, licence line, direct number and the office address set as printed type.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our printer's file. We just want the six agents dropped into it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed face reads as four separate blocks but converts to a frame inventory nothing like that, and the mapping readout of the resulting story omits one printed run entirely while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past it is short by the length of the omitted run. The validator reports the mapping VALID on those wrong offsets and the placeholder step reports success, and only some of the fields actually land.

assets_supplied.name: agent_headshots/ (6 portraits, 3600 x 4800)
assets_supplied.kind: The six agents who work open houses, photographed separately as each joined the firm, most against the office's mottered grey studio wall.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Whatever each agent had. They were all taken here except one."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three were shot against the grey wall in soft light and two of those agents are wearing pale grey jackets, so subject and ground sit within a hair of each other in value along the shoulder line; the knockout returns a clean looking complete cutout and bites the shoulder where the two meet, which is invisible at preview scale and obvious at card scale. One file is a two person crop lifted out of a team photograph, with a second person's arm still in frame.

assets_supplied.name: agent_roster.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Plain CSV: agent name, licence line, direct number, e mail, and a column naming the headshot file for each of the six.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six who work open houses. The licence lines cannot be altered."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The image column holds full paths rather than bare filenames and carries no prefix marker, and two rows spell the same office suite differently.

assets_supplied.name: marlowe_facts.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: address, price, beds, baths, lot size, year, the room list with dimensions, the school district, and the three feature lines the listing agent wants carried.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The facts as they go on the portal. The room list is what the seller signed."

assets_supplied.name: harbor_crest_basis.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of the brokerage's current sign and business card, supplied so the new work does not contradict what is already in the field.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What we already have out there. We are not rebranding, we just want everything to match."

acceptance_bar: The eighteen captures read as one house photographed once when laid in a row at phone scale: one white point, one black point, one neutral for the walls, verticals straight, and rooms sitting at a comparable size in frame. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.

Where a window carries the garden, the view is actually visible in the delivered frame. Where it cannot be, that frame is not passed off as a window shot, and the note says which frames those are and what was done instead.

No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. A tile that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
Every room in the gallery is a different room, and every room the facts sheet names is either present or accounted for in the note.

The six agent cards are one document, one agent per page, in roster order, at the card's true trim, each carrying that agent's own photograph and no one else's, with the licence line reproduced exactly as supplied.
Every field the brokerage expects on the card is actually present on every page. A card that renders successfully with a field missing fails.
On the cards the agent's shoulder line is clean at card scale, not only at preview scale, and no second person appears anywhere on any card.

The one pager, the A4 flyer and the three social canvases are delivered as a native editable document with each canvas keeping its own size, with live retypeable text, a real table for the facts, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference.
One type system across every canvas and the card, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
The whole kit reads as a 625,000 dollar family home in Rosewood: warm, legible, honest. Neither prestige restraint nor a discount shout.

The note records per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, the room reconciliation against the facts sheet, and what the brokerage should watch when they run the next listing through the same kit.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_highlights, image_adjust_light_portions, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision. It fixes one house target off the best daylight frame and brings each of the eighteen to it one call at a time, works the highlight end where the garden has to come back through a window, confines corrections by selecting materials by their own visual properties rather than by the room they sit in, cuts the hero, gallery, flyer and social crops without ever enlarging, and knocks the six agent portraits onto the card's ground with the route chosen per portrait rather than once for all six.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template with params.mappingJson passed as a JSON string, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles, document_render_layout at real resolution
adobe_surfaces.role: The six agent open house cards as a genuine record per page run built from the printer's own PDF, which is the only surface in the connector that does variable data at volume. It requires reverse engineering the flat artwork into a live template, reconstructing the true story text from the round tripped IDML rather than trusting the readout, binding the prepared headshots per row through an image column, and rendering at real print resolution because the merge step ignores resolution on its own.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The listing one pager, the A4 print flyer at true physical dimensions, and the three social canvases as one native editable document with each root declaring its own canvas, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the facts go in as a real table, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload goes by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend called once per typographic role, font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The one type system that has to carry a phone sized listing page, a printed A4 flyer, three social canvases and a printed card. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land warm and legible rather than prestige or shouty. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the brokerage does not have, a neighbourhood or street context band for the wide social canvas, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the selects set the listing agent and the seller sign off from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The photography is raster work with a portal spec, the collateral has to be an authored fixed canvas document because the brokerage rebuilds it every listing, and the six cards are a record per page run that only the merge surface does. The brief pins each destination, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which room and which agent.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eighteen captures and read them against the facts sheet: which room each shows, which are duplicates, which named room has no frame, the illuminant per frame, the verticals, and where a window carries the garden.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts a room by room pass. The pictures are the only place that can settle whether that is eighteen different rooms, and counting files is not the same as reading them.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering room identity, illuminant, tilt, and which frames the sale actually depends on.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the room and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and on interiors a converging vertical is the single tell that reads as amateur at phone scale.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one house target off the best daylight frame and bring each of the eighteen toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eighteen good rooms. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for rooms lit by different windows at different hours, so the agent holds one destination and reaches it by different routes.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen corrected masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Work the highlight end on the frames where the window carries the garden, reading what actually changed in each result rather than the response.
trajectory.judgement: The garden through the glass is the reason this house sells, so the window frames are where the money is and where the agent has to look hardest at its own output.
trajectory.produces: Window frames worked toward the view, each with what moved and what did not recorded.

trajectory.action: Confined corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong: the lawn, the wood floors reading orange, the one cool bedroom, selecting each by the material's own visual properties rather than by the room it sits in.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate. Naming the room pulls the selection to the room; naming the material's colour, surface and form pulls it to the material.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have taken the lawn acid or the walls green.

trajectory.action: Knock the six agent portraits out for the card's ground, reading every returned tradeoffs object rather than the success message, and inspect each cutout at the size the card actually prints it.
trajectory.judgement: Six portraits shot years apart are not one job repeated six times. The tradeoffs array is the only channel reporting what the tool did to the frame, and it carries no warning language.
trajectory.produces: Six agent plates on the card's ground with their returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut every crop the kit needs from the corrected masters: the one pager hero, the gallery tiles, the flyer hero, the three social ratios, and the card's photo frame ratio, room optically placed rather than geometrically centred.
trajectory.judgement: A room is not centred the way a bottle is: the crop has to keep the floor line and the ceiling honest, and a portal that shows a gallery in a strip punishes inconsistent framing more than it punishes a mediocre single frame.
trajectory.produces: The full crop set at spec, each recorded against its source frame's dimensions.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the street or neighbourhood context band, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it to the house target.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the house target, not the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a 625,000 dollar family home and a first move up buyer reading on a phone. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's card PDF, export the IDML, and read the real frame inventory and the real story text before promising any mapping.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed face looks like says nothing about what the conversion exposes, and the mapping strategy is entirely different for separated blocks than for one continuous flow. Looking first is the only honest way to justify a mapping.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with integer page item ids, bounds and applied type, plus the story text reconstructed from the IDML content runs.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the reconstructed story text, run it through the validator, prepare the merge template, then round trip the IDML again and confirm every expected placeholder is actually present in the story.
trajectory.judgement: Neither a VALID verdict nor a success message is evidence that a mapping landed, so the only proof is the placeholder appearing in the re exported story. The image column also has to be reshaped before it can bind anything.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been confirmed by inspection rather than by response text.

trajectory.action: Merge the six agents one record per page with the prepared headshots bound per row, then render at real print resolution through the render step and check each page against its roster row.
trajectory.judgement: The merge step ignores resolution on its own, and multi record raster output cannot be trusted to come back in row order, so identity is established by the route chosen rather than by the position of a link in a list.
trajectory.produces: One press document of six cards in roster order plus per record proofs, each verified against its row.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the listing one pager, the A4 flyer at true physical dimensions and the three social canvases as separate roots, each declaring its own canvas size, with every photograph inlined as image data, the facts as a real table, and family and weight declared on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much air a warm mid market kit carries and how the feature table reads on a phone.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole collateral set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard, so looking at the first canvas is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the others.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the corrected set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the note has to be specific enough that the brokerage can run listing forty one through the same kit without repeating the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the window frames still have anything behind the glass. The client's whole case for the house is the garden through the windows, and on some of these interiors the room was exposed for the room, so the window is clipped flat with no data under it. A highlight recovery pass on those frames returns success and the readout is that nothing moves at all: the result comes back, it is a valid image, and it is indistinguishable from the input. Which frames those are is a property of how each room was metered and is not visible by looking at the thumbnail, because a merely bright window and a dead one look identical until something is asked of them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the information does not exist in the file and no response says so. Nothing states it either: the brief asks that the windows show the garden, which is the client's goal, not a disclosure that five specific frames cannot deliver it. And the response is not a re run of the same chain, it is a different route decided per frame, either recomposing the crop so the dead window falls outside it, or selecting the window region by its own visual properties and treating it as a deliberate flat panel, or dropping the frame and re choosing which rooms carry the gallery at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re decide which rooms carry the one pager gallery and which carries the flyer hero, re cut those crops from different masters, and re balance the corrected set so the substituted rooms still agree with their neighbours, then record in the note which windows could not be brought back.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A listing page whose hero and gallery are built on windows that are blank white rectangles, on a house whose entire selling point is the view through them, delivered with every tool call reporting success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually is once it is a document rather than a printed page. Its frame granularity is not under anyone's control and does not follow the visual blocks, and worse, the readout of the resulting story omits one printed run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly the length of the run that vanished. The validator returns VALID on those wrong offsets with no warnings, and the placeholder step then reports completed successfully. Nothing in any response distinguishes a mapping that landed from one that silently dropped half its fields.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not help, because the omission is a property of this document and is only discoverable by comparing the readout against the story text reconstructed from the round tripped IDML, which nothing instructs and no response hints at. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer holds the artwork and the agents need dropping in. And it is not a propagation re run, because the fix is to recompute every offset from a different source of truth and re prepare the template, then prove the placeholders by inspection rather than by response text.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Recompute all offsets from the reconstructed story, rebuild the mapping, re prepare the template, round trip the IDML again to confirm each placeholder is present, and only then re merge and re render the six cards.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six cards that print cleanly with the licence line or the direct number simply absent, ordered in quantity by a brokerage that read a success message and a VALID verdict as proof.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the knockout holds on the specific portraits shot against the office wall. On the agents wearing pale grey against that mottled grey ground, subject and ground sit within a hair of each other in value along the shoulder line, so the tool returns a clean, complete, entirely plausible cutout that has quietly bitten into the shoulder where the two meet. It looks correct at preview scale and it is only wrong at the size the card prints the photograph. Which portraits do this is a property of each individual frame's own contrast, not of the shoot.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that avoids it, no parameter that controls it, and no response field that reports it, and doing it right first time would mean routing all six through the slower material selection chain on the assumption that some will fail, which is a guess rather than a decision. Nothing states it: the client says only that the portraits were taken at different times. And the fix is a different chain for the affected portraits, selecting the wall by its own material properties, inverting, and filling to the card ground, not the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re route the affected portraits through a material selection, re derive those agent plates, re bind them into the merge, and re render and re inspect those cards at card scale rather than at preview scale.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Open house cards handed out at the door on which two agents have a slice taken out of a shoulder, on the one piece of collateral whose entire job is to make the agent look like a professional.

deliverables.name: 14 Marlowe Crescent listing photography
deliverables.spec: The full room by room set brought to one house target: one white point, one black point, one neutral for the walls, verticals straight, rooms at a comparable size in frame, with the windows carrying the garden wherever the file allows it. One licensed camera scale context frame graded into the same world. Delivered with a per frame parameter log, the room reconciliation against the facts sheet, and a named list of any frame that could not be brought to the set.

deliverables.name: Harbor Crest agent plates
deliverables.spec: The six open house agents isolated onto the card's ground at the card's photograph ratio, edge holding at card scale rather than at preview scale, no second person anywhere in any plate, every output at or below its source dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each. One cut logic across all six, not six separate solutions.

deliverables.name: Open house card run, six agents
deliverables.spec: Six cards, one agent per page, in roster order, at the card's true trim, built from the printer's own artwork rather than a redrawn approximation: each carrying that agent's own photograph bound per record, the licence line reproduced exactly as supplied, and every expected field confirmed present by inspecting the template's story rather than by a success message. Delivered as one press document plus per record proofs at real print resolution.

deliverables.name: Listing collateral: one pager, A4 flyer and social set
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying the listing one pager, the A4 open house flyer at true physical dimensions and the three social canvases, each root keeping its own canvas size, with live retypeable text in one licensed type system, the facts as a real table, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self contained source HTML, which is the durable half: the brokerage rebuilds this every listing and the source is what guarantees the design survives.

deliverables.name: Brokerage basis note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported with the frame it applied to, which windows could not be brought back and what was done instead, what the card template actually contained versus what it appeared to contain, and what to watch on the next listing. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board carrying the corrected set and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source frame it derives from.
verifiers_auto.how: For every delivered file read its pixel dimensions and compare against its named source in the manifest: no capture-derived file may exceed 6000x4000 px, no headshot- or agent-plate-derived file may exceed 3600x4800 px, and no context-frame-derived file may exceed the licensed Stock download's own dimensions.
